source: MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture, បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះដំណាំចេក (Techniques for Banana Cultivation), 2019, section II (អំពីពូជ)
text:
Chek Ambong (ចេកអំបង) is the most widely grown and commercially important variety in Cambodia, accepted both domestically and for export. It grows to a pseudostem height of about 3-6m, has dark green, wax-coated leaf sheaths, and produces round, uniform bunches that turn yellow and develop thin skin and a sweet, fragrant flesh when ripe. A bunch commonly has around 6 hands, though some can have up to 11. This variety is seedless and is noted as being relatively resistant to certain leaf diseases, though it is one of the varieties affected by Fusarium wilt.

Chek Ambong Khsae (ចេកអំបងខ្សែ) is a closely related type, similarly widespread and exported, with dark green wax-coated sheaths that also turn yellow at ripeness; it is valued for good eating quality.

Chek Pong Moan (ចេកពងមាន, "hen's egg banana") is a tall-growing type with thinner, non-waxy green pseudostem sheaths, producing small round bunches with thin skin at ripeness. It is seedless and noted for relatively good resistance to Fusarium wilt, and it tolerates being grown near ponds and waterlogged edges better than some other types, though its roots can extend to around 50cm deep and it still needs consistent watering.

Chek Nam Va (ចេកណាំវា) is popular in cooler upland provinces; it is noted for good wind tolerance and strong water uptake, making it a reasonable choice in exposed or breezy sites.

Chek Ronea (ចេកណាវីេវា / Chek Rachhung Dei Neang, "lady's fingernail banana") is a smaller-statured type with a short pseudostem and small, seedless, sweet-smelling fruit; it is popular in Thailand as well as Cambodia.

Overall, the source notes there are many other named local and introduced varieties beyond these, and that choice of variety should be matched to local climate, soil, market demand, and the farmer's tolerance for disease risk (particularly Fusarium wilt, which affects certain popular varieties more than others).
